report_name: Dutch Security Institute Hacked via AI-Powered Zammad Zero-Days

threat_actors.name: Unnamed Agentic AI Attacker
threat_actors.description: A sophisticated threat actor who compromised the Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure (DIVD) using what was described as an "agentic AI-powered attack." This suggests the use of an autonomous or semi-autonomous agent to chain two zero-day exploits with high speed and minimal human intervention.

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: The attacker exploited an unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-102489) in the public-facing Zammad helpdesk software to gain initial access.

attack_patterns.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
attack_patterns.description: After gaining initial access, the attacker exploited a local privilege escalation vulnerability (CVE-2026-102490) to elevate their privileges to root, gaining full control of the server.

attack_patterns.name: Browser Session Hijacking
attack_patterns.description: The initial RCE vulnerability, CVE-2026-102489, also enabled session hijacking capabilities on the Zammad helpdesk system.

attack_patterns.name: Unix Shell
attack_patterns.description: The attacker likely spawned shells such as 'sh' or 'bash' from the compromised Zammad application server process to execute commands.

attack_patterns.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
attack_patterns.description: The attacker may have used network utilities like 'curl' or 'wget', spawned from the Zammad server, to download additional tools or payloads.

attack_patterns.name: Web Shell
attack_patterns.description: The attacker may have placed a web shell in the Zammad installation directory to maintain persistent access and execute commands.

tools.name: curl
tools.description: The attacker may have used the curl utility, spawned from the compromised Zammad server, for network-related activities such as data transfer.

tools.name: wget
tools.description: The attacker may have used the wget utility, spawned from the compromised Zammad server, to download additional payloads or tools.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-102489
vulnerabilities.description: An unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE) and session hijacking vulnerability in Zammad helpdesk software, which was chained with another vulnerability to achieve full system compromise.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-102490
vulnerabilities.description: A local privilege escalation (LPE) vulnerability in Zammad helpdesk software, used to escalate privileges to root after initial access was gained via CVE-2026-102489.

identities.name: Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure (DIVD)
identities.description: A non-profit security organization that was the victim of a sophisticated cyberattack exploiting two zero-day vulnerabilities in its Zammad helpdesk software.

identities.name: Zammad
identities.description: The vendor of the open-source helpdesk software that contained the two zero-day vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-102489, CVE-2026-102490) exploited in the attack against DIVD.

infrastructure.name: Attacker C2 Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: A compromised Zammad server may initiate outbound connections to an attacker's command and control infrastructure for data exfiltration or to receive further commands.

indicators.name: Zammad Server Spawning Suspicious Child Process
indicators.pattern:
title: Zammad Server Spawning Suspicious Child Process
id: 2a9b3c4d-e5f6-4a90-8bcd-ef1234567890
status: experimental
description: Detects the Zammad application server process (e.g., Puma) spawning shells or network utilities, which could indicate remote code execution.
references:
  - https://www.securityweek.com/zammad-zero-days-exploited-in-ai-powered-divd-hack/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-01
tags:
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1105
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|contains: '/puma'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/sh'
      - '/bash'
      - '/curl'
      - '/wget'
  condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate administrative scripts or integrations that spawn these processes from Zammad.
indicators.description: Detects the Zammad application server process spawning shells or network utilities, which is a strong indicator of compromise via RCE.

indicators.name: Potential Zammad Web Shell Creation
indicators.pattern:
title: Potential Zammad Web Shell Creation
id: 8f7e6d5c-4b3a-4928-9176-c0d1e2f3a4b5
status: experimental
description: Detects the creation of files with common web shell extensions in the Zammad installation directory.
references:
  - https://www.securityweek.com/zammad-zero-days-exploited-in-ai-powered-divd-hack/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-01
tags:
  - attack.t1505.003
level: medium
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|startswith: '/opt/zammad/'
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '.php'
      - '.jsp'
      - '.aspx'
      - '.pl'
      - '.cgi'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate application updates or plugin installations.
indicators.description: Detects the creation of potential web shells within the Zammad application directory, a common post-exploitation technique.
